questions.stem: Which patients may have a posterior femoral cutaneous nerve block for analgesia?
options: Patients undergoing hip replacement through a posterior approach
Patients with chronic low back pain from disc disease
Burns patients with skin graft donor sites on the posterior thigh
Patients undergoing ankle fracture fixation

questions.stem: With which block is a posterior femoral cutaneous nerve block combined for a specific procedure?
options: Hip fracture fixation
Short saphenous vein stripping
Hallux valgus correction
Anterior cruciate ligament repair

questions.stem: Which skin area does the posterior femoral cutaneous nerve supply?
options: Posterior thigh, between lateral and anterior femoral cutaneous areas
Medial thigh, over the obturator nerve territory
Anterior thigh, over the femoral nerve territory
Sole of the foot, over the tibial nerve territory

questions.stem: Which dorsal and ventral sacral rami contribute to the posterior femoral cutaneous nerve?
questions.answer: Dorsal branches of S1 and S2, and ventral branches of S2 and S3

questions.stem: Through which opening does the posterior femoral cutaneous nerve leave the pelvis?
options: Obturator canal, beside the femoral vessels
Greater sciatic foramen, below piriformis
Lesser sciatic foramen, below obturator internus
Inguinal canal, above the inguinal ligament

questions.stem: Relative to the sciatic nerve, where does the posterior femoral cutaneous nerve descend in the buttock?
options: Anterior or lateral to the sciatic nerve
Within the sciatic nerve sheath itself
Superficial to gluteus maximus, lateral to it
Behind or medial to the sciatic nerve

questions.stem: How does the posterior femoral cutaneous nerve run down the back of the thigh?
options: Superficial to the fascia lata, down the front of the thigh
Deep to the fascia lata, down the back of the thigh
Alongside the femoral artery in the adductor canal
Within the sciatic nerve sheath, down the leg

questions.stem: Which regions do all branches of the posterior femoral cutaneous nerve supply?
questions.answer: Gluteal region, perineum, flexor surface of thigh and leg

questions.stem: In which patient positions can a posterior femoral cutaneous nerve block be performed?
options: Prone only, with the leg extended straight
Prone, lateral, or supine with the leg raised 90 degrees
Supine only, with the leg flat on the bed
Sitting upright with the head flexed forward

questions.stem: In the subgluteal approach, what volume is given subcutaneously as a skin wheal at the gluteal fold?
options: 5 mL
20 mL
10 mL
15 mL

questions.stem: In the subgluteal approach, what volume is injected deeper at the midpoint of the gluteal crease?
options: 20 mL
5 mL
15 mL
2 mL

questions.stem: Why is the deeper subgluteal injection fanned out at the midpoint of the gluteal crease?
questions.answer: To reach the nerve before it pierces the deep fascia

questions.stem: Which approach is used to block the posterior femoral cutaneous nerve above the knee?
options: Ankle approach
Lateral thigh approach
Midthigh approach
Retroperitoneal approach

questions.stem: In the midthigh approach, where is the 10 mL subcutaneous injection placed?
options: Along a line 5 cm above and parallel to the popliteal crease
Along a line 5 cm below the gluteal fold
Over the fibular head, 5 cm distally
Over the greater trochanter, 10 cm proximally
